### Load packages and data

```{r load-packages, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```


## Load & join data sets

```{r load-data, message = FALSE}
# Member 2 (pair 1) write code to load File 1 data here:
data1 <- read_csv("data/mismanaged-plastic-waste-per-capita.csv")


# Member 4 (pair 2) write code to load File 2 data here:
data2 <- read_csv2("data/per-capita-ocean-plastic-waste.txt")


# Member 1 (pair 1) write code to load File 3 data here:
data3 <- read_tsv("data/UN_country_population.tsv")


# Member 3 (pair 2) write code to load File 4 data here:
data4 <- read_excel("data/UN_country_region.xlsx")



```



```{r join-data, message = FALSE}
# Member 2 (pair 1) write code to create object 'plastic_data_all':
plastic_data_all <- data1



# Member 4 (pair 2) write code to join your data to 'plastic_data_all':
plastic_data_all <- data2 %>%
  select(-name) %>%
  left_join(plastic_data_all, by = "code")


# Member 1 (pair 1) write code to join your data to 'plastic_data_all':
plastic_data_all <- data3 %>%
  select(-name) %>%
  right_join(plastic_data_all, by = "code")



# Member 3 (pair 2) write code to join your data to 'plastic_data_all':
plastic_data_all <- data4 %>%
  select(-name) %>%
  right_join(plastic_data_all, by = "code")

```


```{r print-data, message = FALSE}
# Member 2 (pair 1) adds code here to view the first 10 rows of 'plastic_data_all'
plastic_data_all %>% head(n = 10)


```



## Exercises

### Ex 1.

```{r Ex1, message = FALSE}
# Write your code here to answer exercise 1
coastal_countries <- (left_join(data2, data4, by = c("name", "code"))) 
coastal_countries |> 
  group_by(region) |> 
  count()
#Africa has the most number of coastal countries/ territories
```



### Ex 2.

```{r Ex2, message = FALSE}
# Write your code here to answer exercise 2
plastic_data_all <- plastic_data_all |> mutate(total_mismanage_plastic = mismanaged_plastic * population)

plastic_data_region_mean <- plastic_data_all |> 
  group_by(region) |> 
  summarise(mean = mean(total_mismanage_plastic, na.rm = TRUE))
plastic_data_region_mean

plastic_data_region_total <- plastic_data_all |> 
  group_by(region) |> 
  summarise(total = sum(total_mismanage_plastic, na.rm = TRUE))

plastic_data_region_total

max_mismanage_plastic <- max(plastic_data_region_total$total, na.rm = TRUE)
min_mismanage_plastic <- min(plastic_data_region_total$total, na.rm = TRUE)

max_min_mismanage_plastic_region <- plastic_data_region_total |>
  filter(total == max_mismanage_plastic | total == min_mismanage_plastic)
max_min_mismanage_plastic_region
```


### Ex 3.

```{r Ex3, message = FALSE}
# Write your code here to answer exercise 3
plastic_data_all <- plastic_data_all |> mutate(pct_mismanaged_plastic_ocean = (mismanaged_plastic_ocean / mismanaged_plastic) * 100) |> 
  drop_na()

pct_plastic_data_region_median <- plastic_data_all |> 
  group_by(region) |> 
  summarise(median = median(pct_mismanaged_plastic_ocean))
pct_plastic_data_region_median

#did not (have to) use na.rm = TRUE as exercise wanted to use drop_na()

min_pct_plastic_data_region_median_value <- min(pct_plastic_data_region_median$median)

min_pct_plastic_data_region_median <- pct_plastic_data_region_median |> 
  filter(median == min_pct_plastic_data_region_median_value)
min_pct_plastic_data_region_median

#Africa has lowest median in ocean mismanaged plastic
```


### Ex 4.

```{r Ex4, message = FALSE}
# Write your code here to answer exercise 4
plastic_data_all <- plastic_data_all %>%
  rename(pop = population,
         reg = region,
         mismanaged = mismanaged_plastic,
         mismanaged_ocean = mismanaged_plastic_ocean,
         total_mismanaged = total_mismanage_plastic,
         pct_mismanaged_ocean = pct_mismanaged_plastic_ocean)

plastic_data_all <- plastic_data_all |> 
  mutate(reg = case_when(
    reg == "Latin America and The Caribbean" ~ "LAC",
    reg == "Africa" ~ "AFR",
    reg == "Asia" ~ "ASI",
    reg == "Oceania"~ "OCE",
    reg == "Europe" ~ "EUR",
    reg == "North America" ~ "NA",
    TRUE ~ reg
    ))

#if mutate using the same variable name, it would replace it, rather than creating a new column with that same name

plastic_data_region <- plastic_data_all |>
  group_by(reg) |> 
  summarise(IQR = IQR(total_mismanaged, na.rm = TRUE))

plastic_data_region

#"interesting" statistic created was IQR of the total mismanaged plastics within regions
```
